findings.title: totalPages off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: The totalPages computed property uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members with limit 50) this returns 3 instead of the correct 2, so showingLast stays false on the real last page and the admin can navigate to an empty trailing page (page 3 of 2). Replace with Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (keeping the user_count == 0 guard) so the pager reflects the actual number of pages.

findings.title: Stray inside the group members table
findings.body:
There is a stray closing tag inside the , sitting between and {{/each}}. A cannot be a direct child of a table outside cell context, so this is invalid HTML; browsers will attempt to repair the DOM, which can shift rendered elements and break the table styling that this PR is also touching. The tag is clearly leftover from an earlier template shape (the surrounding
wrapper was removed in this diff but the close tag was not). Remove the

findings.title: add_members silently drops unknown or whitespace-padded usernames and still reports success
findings.body: In the add_members action the usernames.split(",").each loop silently ignores names that don't resolve via User.find_by_username, and the split does no whitespace stripping, so an entry like " bob" (with a leading space) won't match the stored username and is also dropped. The action then renders success_json regardless of how many names were actually accepted, so the admin sees success even when every supplied username was invalid. Strip each username before lookup, and either reject the request or include the not-found names in the response so the caller can tell which entries failed.

findings.title: add_members crashes with NoMethodError when usernames is sent as an array
findings.body: params.require(:usernames) accepts whatever shape is sent; if a client posts usernames[]=alice&usernames[]=bob (the standard Rails array-param convention), params[:usernames] is an Array. The subsequent usernames.split(",") then raises NoMethodError because Array has no split method, returning a 500 to the caller. Coerce the param to a string before splitting (e.g. Array(params[:usernames]).flatten.join(",")) or return a 400 when the value is not a String.

findings.title: save error handler throws when the server returns an empty or non-JSON error body
findings.body: The save action's rejection handler does var message = $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors; with no guard. When the server returns an empty body, an HTML error page from a proxy (502/504), or any non-JSON content, $.parseJSON throws. The throw escapes the rejection handler and surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection, the bootbox alert is never shown, and the failure is invisible to the admin. Wrap the parse in a try/catch (or check that e.responseText is non-empty and parseable) and fall back to a generic message such as I18n.t('generic_error') when parsing fails.

findings.title: addMembers action carries an unresolved TODO to clear the input
findings.body: The addMembers action still contains the comment // TODO: should clear the input but does not implement it. After a successful add the user-selector continues to show the just-typed usernames, so an admin who wants to add more members has to manually delete the previously typed list. Either reset this.set('usernames', null) (and the bound input) after the AJAX call resolves, or remove the TODO comment.
